sections.h2: Does Florida have an inheritance tax or an estate tax?
sections.html:
No. The Department of Revenue says a federal change eliminated Florida's estate tax for people who died after December 31, 2004, and since July 1, 2023 personal representatives have not had to file Form DR-312 or DR-313 (Florida Department of Revenue, estate tax).

Heirs who receive a Florida house therefore owe no state tax simply for inheriting it. The Florida Revenue page is the place to confirm this if a lender, buyer or relative asks.

Other taxes can still touch a sale of inherited property: the federal estate tax for very large estates, federal income tax on gain, and the state's deed stamp tax when title moves for value. The sections below take each in turn.

sections.h2: When could the federal estate tax apply to a Florida estate?
sections.html:
Only for large estates. The Internal Revenue Service says an estate tax return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, exceeds the filing threshold for the year of death (IRS, estate tax).

The thresholds the agency prints are:

Year of deathFiling threshold
2023$12,920,000
2024$13,610,000
2025$13,990,000
2026$15,000,000

Source: IRS estate tax page, filing threshold table. The estate tax counts everything the decedent owned, at fair market value at death, and allows deductions for debts, administration expenses and property passing to a surviving spouse or qualified charities. Spouses can elect to pass unused exemption to the survivor on a timely filed return.

sections.h2: What basis does an heir get when selling an inherited Florida house?
sections.html:
Usually the value at the date of death rather than what the decedent paid. IRS Publication 551 says the basis of inherited property is generally the fair market value at the moment of death, or on the alternate valuation date if the personal representative chose it (IRS Publication 551).

Two details help heirs. When an estate files Form 706, beneficiaries generally receive a Schedule A (Form 8971) from the executor showing the estate tax value, and some must use it as their starting basis. If no Schedule A arrives, the publication says basis can be determined from the appraised value at death used for state inheritance or transmission tax purposes.

One exception: appreciated property you or your spouse gave the decedent within one year before death does not get the new basis. It keeps the decedent's adjusted basis.

An appraisal near the date of death is worth keeping in the estate file. A CPA can say how basis interacts with your selling price and any gain.

sections.h2: Is income from selling inherited property taxed?
sections.html: Income tax on a sale is a federal question, answered on the heir's own return, and a CPA can say whether any other return applies to you. Selling at or near the date-of-death value usually produces little gain because of the basis rule above. A sale well above it can produce gain, which is a federal matter.

sections.h2: What does Florida charge when an inherited house changes hands?
sections.html:
It depends on how title moves. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable, while taxable deeds include warranty, special warranty, quit claim and life estate deeds (Department of Revenue, documentary stamp tax).

When a deed is taxable, the rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration (60 cents plus a surtax in Miami-Dade), and consideration includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property whether or not assumed. The department adds that there is no specific exemption for documents that transfer Florida real property for estate planning purposes. That is why a gift of a mortgaged house can carry tax even when no money changes hands (Florida Statutes, s. 201.02).

  • A personal representative's deed under a probated will is the untaxed route.
  • Quitclaim deeds between heirs can be taxable if debts attach.
  • All parties to a taxable deed are liable, whichever one agrees to pay.

sections.h2: Which probate rules matter when heirs want to sell a Florida house?
sections.html:
Three statutes set the pace. Summary administration is available if the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the decedent has been dead more than two years (s. 735.201). A creditor's claim is barred unless filed by the later of three months after first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days after service on a creditor who must be served (s. 733.702). And where only exempt or very limited personal property remains, a court may authorize transfer without administration (s. 735.301).

Homestead adds a layer. A homestead cannot be devised when the owner leaves a spouse or minor child, so the will may not decide who holds title, and a surviving spouse has six months to elect a half interest in lieu of a life estate (Florida Statutes, s. 732.401). Find out which documents the title insurer will require before it insures a buyer.

Property tax keeps accruing while the estate is open. Assessment happens each January 1, and a change of ownership by transfer at death resets just value the following January 1 unless a listed exception applies.

sections.h2: What paperwork should heirs have ready for the sale?
sections.html:
Heirs move faster when the file is complete. The list below covers items that come up in most inherited house sales in Florida.

  • A date-of-death appraisal or Schedule A (Form 8971), if the estate issued one, to document basis.
  • The letters or order from the probate court, or a summary administration order, showing who may sign.
  • A recorded notice of election if a surviving spouse chose a half interest in homestead.
  • The most recent tax bill and any deferral paperwork.
  • Proof of how any deed is exempt or taxed under chapter 201.

The Revenue page confirms that estate tax filings under Forms DR-312 and DR-313 are no longer required, so there is no state clearance letter to chase. Federal Form 706 matters only when the gross estate exceeds the IRS threshold for the year of death.

Heirs who cannot agree on a sale price or a buyer may need the court to decide. Raise that early, because a house that sits vacant still generates tax bills, insurance costs and upkeep.

faqs.q: Does Florida have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. The Florida Department of Revenue says estate tax was eliminated for deaths after December 31, 2004, and Florida lists no inheritance levy. Heirs owe no state tax just for receiving a house.

faqs.q: Do I owe federal estate tax on a house I inherit?
faqs.a: Only if the estate exceeds the IRS filing threshold, which is $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths. The estate pays any tax, not the heir directly, and most estates fall below the threshold.

faqs.q: What is my basis if I sell an inherited Florida house?
faqs.a: Generally the fair market value at the moment of death, or the alternate valuation date if the estate used it. If a Schedule A (Form 8971) was issued, it reports the estate tax value for beneficiaries who must use it.

faqs.q: Is there documentary stamp tax on a personal representative's deed?
faqs.a: The state revenue agency lists a personal representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable. Other deeds, such as quit claim or warranty deeds, are taxable at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties.

faqs.q: Who reports the gain when I sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: Any gain is reported on the heir's federal return, and the date-of-death basis generally keeps it small for a prompt sale. A CPA can confirm.
